long_description.before:
At Dataleap we have one single focus - make knowledge work at your computer fun! Give all the other roles in sales, ops, hr the same super powers that engineers get with Cursor and Claude Code. 

Dataleap is the agentic operating system for the Enterprise. We enable business teams to automate they work without any help from engineering. No visual workflow builder, no hour long setup or steep learning curve in n8n. Build your AI coworkers in minutes with a fully agent first interface.
long_description.after:
In a few years, agents will do most of the work in a company, and software will fade into the database underneath. Every employee becomes an agent manager: setting the goal, making the decisions that matter, and steering systems that run around the clock.

Dataleap is the open platform where companies build those agentic systems. Instead of waiting on engineering or stitching together chat windows, teams in sales, operations, finance and HR build systems that run whole processes from start to finish: agents doing the work, a custom app as the cockpit where humans step in, and shared data underneath. Any model, any tool. IT governs all of it from one place with budgets, granular permissions, and a full record of every tool call.

We're a small team in San Francisco and Munich, and our deployment strategists work on site with customers until their teams build without us. Starting from our German roots, leading European scale-ups like EGYM, sennder and CarOnSale already run core parts of their business on Dataleap.

one_liner.after: Build agentic systems that run your business

long_description.before:
One API to search, enrich, and monitor the web.

An agent is only as good as the data it runs on. Most agents and GTM tools today are stuck pulling stale, fragmented data from a dozen different providers, which caps how good their output can ever be. We unify all of it behind one API.

One credit-based API covers people data, company data, web search, deep research, news, social signals, and web scraping. Multi-provider waterfall logic routes each call to the best source and falls back automatically, so you get one integration and one bill instead of stitching together Clay, Apollo, Exa, Tavily, and a handful of others.

We're building the data layer that agents and GTM teams plug into to find, understand, and reach their customers.

long_description.before:
Inference research at the frontier. We make frontier open models faster and cheaper on Wally.

We're RunAnywhere. You can use frontier open models like GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3 on Wally today. Wally has an OpenAI-compatible API and the wally CLI, with zero data retention by default, and it works with OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Cline. Tell your agent: set up https://runanywhere.ai/SKILL.md

Our engineers and AI agents build the kernels and the serving stack for each chip. For AWS Trainium, trnRT is our open-source (Apache-2.0) LLM inference engine; Aman Swar and Sanchit Monga's post covers serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box: https://runanywhere.ai/blog/glm-5-3-flash-trainium2-nki-megakernels

For on-device AI, the open-source RunAnywhere SDKs share a C++ core across Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, TypeScript and C++.

We publish how we measured each result. Happy to help any YC founder running coding agents, long-context workloads or on-device models.
long_description.after:
RunAnywhere does inference research at the frontier. We make frontier open models faster and cheaper to run, and serve them through Wally.

We write the kernels and inference engines that run open models on every chip we touch, from data-center GPUs and AWS Trainium to phones and laptops. Wally puts that work behind one OpenAI-compatible API and CLI, with zero data retention by default, and plugs into coding agents like OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex and Cline.

Our open-source work includes trnRT, an LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium, and the RunAnywhere SDKs for running models on device, with 10,000+ GitHub stars.

long_description.before:
The problem: 
AI has quietly become one of the largest and fastest-growing line items for companies. Spend is scattered across a dozen provider consoles that each show one number at the end of the month and nothing about why it moved. There's no unified view, and no way to trace a dollar back to the customer, feature, team, or even the pull request that caused it.

Which customers are unprofitable once you subtract their AI costs? Which feature is quietly burning your Anthropic budget? Is this week's spike a runaway loop or real growth? How much did that AI-written PR actually cost to ship?
Today teams reverse-engineer answers by exporting CSVs from each provider and stitching them together in a spreadsheet, and by the time they do, the money is already spent.

What SuperPenguin does: SuperPenguin tracks AI spend across 14 providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Modal, Cursor, OpenRouter, and more).

* Zero-code setup: connect an API key and costs sync automatically with model-level breakdowns, trends, and forecasts
* Per-request attribution: add two lines with our Python or TypeScript SDK to tag every AI call by customer, feature, team, or environment (or any other metadata).
* AI coding cost per PR: connect Cursor to see engineering spend attributed to each pull request, repo, and developer, so you know what it actually costs to ship.
* Alerts on budget thresholds and spend anomalies, delivered to Slack, email, or Discord.

Most teams are set up in under five minutes. We help companies see where their AI money goes and whether it's worth it.
long_description.after:
Your product runs the same AI workflows over and over, such as a support answer or a coding agent session. Each run makes several model calls, and some of them don't need to happen: a retry after a timeout, the same context sent again on every turn, an answer that runs to the output limit. One extra call costs cents, but it repeats on every run, and provider consoles show the result only as one monthly total.

SuperPenguin breaks each workflow run into its model calls and what each one cost. It then opens a ticket for each fix with the monthly saving estimated in dollars.

Setup takes two steps. For AI products, wrap your client with our Python or TypeScript SDK and tag calls by customer, feature or team; calls still go straight to your provider. For coding agents, run npx superpenguin to turn on usage tracking for Cursor, Claude Code and Codex.

Spend is also split by customer and feature, spikes trigger an alert in Slack, email or Discord, and tracked spend is checked against each provider's bill.

Start saving money on your AI bills via SuperPenguin

one_liner.before: AI Cost Management: Track and attribute AI spend across every provider
one_liner.after: Cost optimization for AI products and coding agents

long_description.before:
Insurance is one of the last big industries still running on manual work.

Trillions in premium flow through brokers who still have to key the same data into their agency management system (AMS), chase clients for documents, and fill one carrier portal after another.

Every hour spent on manual quoting is an hour not spent selling. Across tens of thousands of brokers, that's billions in revenue left on the table.

Software never fixed it, because the work sits between systems and raters are outdated.

Covera runs it end to end, with AI workflows connected to the AMS, the inbox and 100+ carrier portals. It fits the way brokers already work, so their teams can focus on advising clients and closing business.

In 3 months, Covera went live with 90+ brokers in the US and Europe. Brokers now go from a client's email to a quote in 3 minutes, instead of hours.

Covera is founded by repeat founders Tiphaine Venet and Thibaut Regerat, who previously built and sold Simio, a conversational AI company.
long_description.after:
Covera is the AI quoting system for insurance brokers. 

We started 4 months ago and have already reached $641K ARR, growing 30% week over week. We work with 90+ brokers in the US and Europe, including Howden the world's #9 broker.

We make brokers win 20% more deals. In insurance, the first to quote wins, and Covera takes a quote end to end, from intake to proposal, in under 5 minutes across 200+ carrier portals.

To fill quotes end to end, Covera collectas and learns the insurance know-how behind every quote: dwelling limits, deductibles, coverage options, what each carrier accepts or declines, and at what price. We've seen over 1M quotes in 4 months. This data gives us the best quoting system on the market. It also puts us in the best position to see where risk is underinsured or gets declined, so we can distribute carrier and MGA products and build our own insurance products.

Repeat founders Tiphaine Venet (CEO) and Thibaut Regerat (CTO) met 7 years ago at Pretto, a French insurance and mortgage broker. They then bootstrapped Simio to $3M ARR in 2 years and sold it.

long_description.before: Axonnic is building the missing data layer for dexterous robotics. Our wearable EMG technology captures human intent, effort and force directly from muscle activity as people demonstrate physical tasks. By revealing the physical signals that video cannot capture, Axonnic gives AI models the data they need to learn more precise and dexterous behaviour. Beyond robotics, this creates a foundation for new forms of human–computer interaction in which technology can understand and respond directly to human movement and intent.
